headline: Bangladesh vs Pakistan Asian Games semi-final toss delayed due to wet outfield; 13-over match confirmed
summary: The match was reduced to 13 overs per side after initial delays, with Pakistan winning the toss and opting to field first against Bangladesh.
details: Pakistan won the toss and chose to field first against Bangladesh in the Asian Games cricket semi-final. The match has been reduced to 13 overs per side due to a wet outfield.
The toss was initially delayed despite sunny weather, with umpires conducting multiple inspections. The decision for a 13-over game was made after a final observation.
The delay was crucial as another semi-final between India and Sri Lanka is scheduled for the same ground later today. Any further postponement would have impacted the subsequent match.

Both teams' quarter-final matches were washed out by rain, with Bangladesh and Pakistan advancing based on their higher rankings. Today's weather forecast was sunny, and Bangladesh had practiced under similar conditions yesterday.
If the match had been called off entirely, Pakistan would have automatically qualified for the final due to their superior ranking. However, officials were confident the game would proceed today.

headline_marked: [[PM Tarique orders release of teacher]] detained over alleged derogatory remarks in Kushtia
headline: PM Tarique orders release of teacher detained over alleged derogatory remarks in Kushtia
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed displeasure over the detention of a school teacher in Kushtia for alleged derogatory remarks, directing police to release him. He emphasized respect for freedom of expression and differing views as strengths of democracy
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman directed police to release a school teacher detained in Kushtia for alleged derogatory remarks about him, according to PM's adviser Mahdi Amin. The Prime Minister was reportedly upset upon learning of the detention and ensured the teacher's safe return home.

In a Facebook post, Mahdi Amin stated that the Prime Minister believes people are entitled to their own opinions and that freedom of expression should be respected, even when there is disagreement. He added that mutual respect and coexistence strengthen society.

The teacher, Golam Kibria Lalon, who teaches Bangla at Pragpur Secondary School in Daulatpur upazila, was detained on Wednesday. The incident reportedly occurred during a Class 10 Bangla lesson on Tuesday afternoon.

Students alleged that Lalon commented on the Prime Minister’s Bangla pronunciation in his recent speech at the UN General Assembly and later made objectionable remarks while referring to him. This angered students, who informed their guardians, leading to a gathering at the school demanding action.

Police intervened to control the situation and detained Lalon from the Bheramara-Pragpur regional highway. Headteacher Ashrafuzzaman Mukul stated that Lalon denied making derogatory remarks during questioning.
caption:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman ordered the immediate release of a teacher detained in Kushtia for alleged derogatory remarks about him.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman directed police to release a school teacher detained in Kushtia for alleged derogatory remarks about him, according to PM's adviser Mahdi Amin. The Prime Minister was reportedly upset upon learning of the detention and ensured the teacher's safe return home.

In a Facebook post, Mahdi Amin stated that the Prime Minister believes people are entitled to their own opinions and that freedom of expression should be respected, even when there is disagreement. He added that mutual respect and coexistence strengthen society.

The teacher, Golam Kibria Lalon, who teaches Bangla at Pragpur Secondary School in Daulatpur upazila, was detained on Wednesday. The incident reportedly occurred during a Class 10 Bangla lesson on Tuesday afternoon.

Students alleged that Lalon commented on the Prime Minister’s Bangla pronunciation in his recent speech at the UN General Assembly and later made objectionable remarks while referring to him. This angered students, who informed their guardians, leading to a gathering at the school demanding action.

Police intervened to control the situation and detained Lalon from the Bheramara-Pragpur regional highway. Headteacher Ashrafuzzaman Mukul stated that Lalon denied making derogatory remarks during questioning.
